# sample

`axis`, `button`, `frame`, `motion`, `ring`, `sample`, `touch`, and `trigger` define device-neutral gamepad input samples, diagnostics, and bounded frame transport for `gamepad::unstable::controller`.

## Contents

### Stick and Trigger Types

- [axis.hpp](./axis.hpp) exports `stick`, `stick_count`, `stick_vector`, `stick_raw`, and `stick_sample` for normalized, raw, calibrated, and filtered stick stages.
- [axis.cpp](./axis.cpp) implements `to_string(stick)` and `stick_vector::magnitude()`.
- [trigger.hpp](./trigger.hpp) exports `trigger_side`, `trigger_count`, and `trigger_sample` for analog trigger readings.
- [trigger.cpp](./trigger.cpp) implements `to_string(trigger_side)`.

### Buttons

- [button.hpp](./button.hpp) exports the physical-position `button` enum and constexpr, allocation-free `button_set`.
- [button.cpp](./button.cpp) implements `to_string(button)` with stable lowercase hyphenated identifiers.

### Samples and Sensors

- [sample.hpp](./sample.hpp) exports `battery_state`, `raw_sample`, and `canonical_sample`.
- [sample.cpp](./sample.cpp) implements `to_string(battery_state::status)`.
- [motion.hpp](./motion.hpp) exports `sensor_vec3`, `gyro_sample`, `accel_sample`, and `motion_sample`.
- [touch.hpp](./touch.hpp) exports `touch_point` and `touchpad`.

### Frames and Transport

- [frame.hpp](./frame.hpp) exports timestamped `input_frame` values containing device identity, connection state, sequence ordering, timing, and `canonical_sample`.
- [frame.cpp](./frame.cpp) implements diagnostic `operator<<(ostream&, const input_frame&)`.
- [ring.hpp](./ring.hpp) exports the templated SPSC `frame_ring<Capacity>` queue.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`raw_sample` retains device-native values, `canonical_sample` converts them into device-neutral `button_set`, `stick_sample`, `trigger_sample`, `touchpad`, `motion_sample`, `battery_state`, and `capabilities`, and `input_frame` orders canonical samples with `sequence` and `latency_span timing`.

`frame_ring<Capacity>` transfers `input_frame` values from one producer to one consumer, while `stick_sample::filtered` supplies the gameplay input stage.

## Behavioral Contracts

- `stick_vector::magnitude()` computes `sqrt(x*x + y*y)`.
- `stick_vector` components target `[-1, 1]`, while magnitude may exceed `1` before radial clamping.
- `button_set::mask` maps each button to `uint32_t {1} << static_cast<uint32_t>(b)`.
- `button_set::pressed_since(button_set prev)` detects current-down/previous-up edges, and `released_since(button_set prev)` detects current-up/previous-down edges.
- `to_string(button)` returns lowercase hyphenated labels such as `"face-south"`, `"dpad-up"`, and `"edge-paddle-left"`; unknown values and `button::count` return `"count"`.
- `to_string(stick)` and `to_string(trigger_side)` return `"left"` or `"right"`; unknown values fall back to `"left"`.
- `to_string(battery_state::status)` returns `"unknown"`, `"discharging"`, `"charging"`, or `"full"`; unknown values fall back to `"unknown"`.
- `trigger_sample::raw` retains `0..255` units, and `trigger_sample::normalized` stores post-deadzone `[0,1]` values.
- `battery_state::percent` stores `0..100` when reported, while empty `optional` values preserve absent capability state.
- `touchpad::max_points` equals `2`; inactive `touch_point` fields are stale.
- `frame_ring<Capacity>` requires `Capacity >= 2` with `"a ring needs at least two slots to distinguish states"`.
- `frame_ring<Capacity>` requires `(Capacity & (Capacity - 1)) == 0` with `"ring capacity must be a power of two"`.
- `frame_ring<Capacity>::push` drops newest frames when `h - t >= Capacity`, and `try_pop` reports empty state when `t == h`.
- `frame_ring<Capacity>::push` asserts `f.sequence > last_sequence_ || h == 0`.
- `input_frame::sequence` increases monotonically per device, and `latency_span::latency()` is meaningful only after `timing.consumed` is stamped.

## File Relationships

`sample.hpp` composes `axis.hpp`, `button.hpp`, `trigger.hpp`, `touch.hpp`, `motion.hpp`, and `capability.hpp` types into `raw_sample` and `canonical_sample`.

`frame.hpp` composes `device_id`, `family`, `connection`, `latency_span`, and `canonical_sample` into `input_frame`, while `frame.cpp` formats `input_frame` diagnostics.

`ring.hpp` stores fixed-inline `array<input_frame, Capacity>` values and publishes `head_` and `tail_` with acquire/release SPSC synchronization.
